title: Culinary Arts Level I Foundational Skills
award: Certificate of Achievement requiring 8S/12Q to fewer than 16S/24Q units

program.section_heading: Culinary Arts Level I Foundational Skills Certificate
outcomes: Practice the principles of sanitation and food safety to prevent the spread of food-borne illness.
Practice and understand culinary fundamentals that include cooking methods, food quality discernment, preparation techniques, flavor development, sensory evaluation, and recipe literacy.
Manage and make informed business decisions to control costs and promote profitability.
Understand and practice human resource management principles.
Understand how to communicate, prepare, plan, and execute food and service that is nutritionally mindful.
Understand advanced cooking methods that include sous vide, molecular gastronomy, charcuterie, restaurant-style cooking and their applications in various food service establishments and settings.
Understand domestic and international food cultures, traditions, norms, authenticity, ingredients, preparations, and techniques.
Identify the food-service industry’s styles of service and the functions of service personnel.
Understand the functions of beverage management and basic principles of food and beverage pairings.
Work as a team member and leader to achieve common goals and objectives.

notes: The catalog prints codes without a space (CUL101, CUL102, CUL103A, CUL104); these match closed-list CUL 101, CUL 102, CUL 103A, CUL 104, so none is a catalog addition.

The program learning outcomes are printed for the program as a whole; several (e.g., advanced cooking methods, beverage management, human resource management) appear broader than this four-course Level I certificate, so they may be shared across the culinary program.
The description mentions 'employment or promotion within the culinary industry' but names no specific career or job title; careers left empty.
